cubes.text: The TV glows in the dark, and you’re sprawled across the couch when she appears, arms crossed under her chest, her robe loose.
Can I sit with you a little?
Always. They’re showing one of those romantic movies you like.
Good. I couldn’t sleep. Kept tossing, so I figured I’d come keep you company instead.
I’m sorry if it’s because of me.
No, darling. It’s not your fault. You’ve been going through so much, and sometimes I don’t know what to do or how to react. But I know one thing: I love you, and that won’t change. Ever.
Her top has slipped lower than it usually sits, exposing a soft shadow of cleavage. You try to be respectful, but your eyes wander. She doesn’t pull the fabric up or call you out.
Thanks, {{mom}} . I need you to know I’m not doing this on purpose. You’re the most important person in my life.

She leans into you, and you both face the television, her head against your shoulder. The movie hums on, but your focus drifts between the actors and the warm curve of her chest rising and falling with each breath. She’s caught you—more than once—yet she stays quiet, letting you look, letting the silence say what neither of you dares to voice.
